title: Practice 9: Which prefix? — the whole table, as practice

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: This river is dangerous to swim across.
exercises.why: **переплывать** (the infinitive) (to swim across; to sail across) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **переплыть**. — Wiktionary, «переплывать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **отплывать** (**отплывать**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **приплывать** (**приплывать**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **уплывать** (**уплывать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom got off the plane.
exercises.why: **вышел** is the past tense (masculine) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. past: он вы́шел · она вы́шла · оно вы́шло · они вы́шли. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **вошёл** (**войти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **сошёл** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards; **ушёл** (**уйти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He made me cry.
exercises.why: **довёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **довести** (to lead, to take, to accompany (to), to bring (into); (cooking) to scald) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **доводить**. past: он довёл · она довела́ · оно довело́ · они довели́. — Wiktionary, «довести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **обвёл** (**обвести**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **отвёл** (**отвести**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **привёл** (**привести**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Look! The airplane is taking off.
exercises.why: **взлетает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **взлетать** (to fly up, to soar, to take off, to take wing; (figurative) to zoom) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **взлететь**. present: я взлета́ю · ты взлета́ешь · он взлета́ет · мы взлета́ем · вы взлета́ете · они взлета́ют. — Wiktionary, «взлетать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вз-, взо-, воз-, вс-, вос-** — Movement upwards. Antonym: с- Example: Альпинист взошёл на гору. — The mountain climber walked up the mountain. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **влетает** (**влетать**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **облетает** (**облетать**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **подлетает** (**подлетать**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He passed among the crowd.
exercises.why: **прошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **пройти** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. past: он прошёл · она прошла́ · оно прошло́ · они прошли́. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **дошёл** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **перешёл** (**перейти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **сошёл** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: An old woman is walking across the road.
exercises.why: **переходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **переходить** (to cross, to get over, to get across; to pass on (to), to proceed (to), to turn (to)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **перейти**. present: я перехожу́ · ты перехо́дишь · он перехо́дит · мы перехо́дим · вы перехо́дите · они перехо́дят. — Wiktionary, «переходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. exercises.q: Tom is out of the race.
exercises.why: **сошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **сойти** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сходить**. past: он сошёл · она сошла́ · оно сошло́ · они сошли́. — Wiktionary, «сойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **дошёл** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **отошёл** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **ушёл** (**уйти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Tom got out of the limo.
exercises.why: **вылез** is the past tense (masculine) of **вылезть** (to get out, to climb out, to get off; (of hair) to fall out, to come out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вылезать**. past: он вы́лез · она вы́лезла · оно вы́лезло · они вы́лезли. — Wiktionary, «вылезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. exercises.q: I took the children to school.
exercises.why: **отвёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **отвести** (to lead away; to take / draw aside) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отводить**. past: он отвёл · она отвела́ · оно отвело́ · они отвели́. — Wiktionary, «отвести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  «отводить — отвести — to take (lead) to. Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there". Thus:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there".» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я отвёл сына в школу.» (I took (walked with) my son to school.) — DLI, Lesson 79. exercises.q: We ran around the park.
exercises.why: **обежали** is the past tense (plural) of **обежать** (to run around [with accusative or вокру́г (vokrúg, + genitive) ‘a location’]; to run [with ми́мо (mímo, + genitive) ‘past a location’] (to bypass while running)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **обегать**. past: он обежа́л · она обежа́ла · оно обежа́ло · они обежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «обежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**о-, об-, обо-** — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place Example: Девочка обошла лужу. — The little girl walked around the puddle. Я обхожу все магазины в центре. — I'm going around to all the stores in the mall. Prepositional phrases: вокруг + gen.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "об-" indicates a motion around a place and may mean: a) Circling a place. The verb is followed by the preposition вокруг + Gen.: Самолёт облетел вокруг аэродрома. Я хочу объехать вокруг озера. b) Making a detour. No preposition is used; the verb is followed by the Accusative case: Мы объехали это место. Противник обошёл наш город. c) Making the rounds of … or going all over … No preposition is used; the verb is followed by the Accusative case: Я обошёл все магазины. — I made the rounds of all the stores. Я обошёл весь город. — I walked all over town.» — DLI, Lesson 62.
